title: Describing his own playing and early influences
summary: Prez, Getz, Mulligan, Rollins, Coltrane and Johnny Hodges shaped his sound.

blocks.x: Yeah I want to talk about that a bit later. I was reading in the Grove Dictionary of Jazz there’s an entry on you and your brothers. And I was going to read — you know it’s a challenge, they try to describe musicians’ styles, sometimes in one sentence for space reasons. And I was going to read what they said about you but I’m thinking how would you like an opportunity to describe your own playing and in about twenty words. Can you do that?

Well my playing comes from — the earliest references that I referenced were basically Gerry Mulligan, Prez, Stan Getz, Sonny Rollins, Coltrane. I mean I listened to all those guys. Lester Young was a huge influence on me and even to this day, I went through all the periods of music listening to everybody, studied with everybody that I could. And you know, playing with Elvin you had to play a certain way, or I felt that I did, or more modern, but even now today I go back to Lester Young and the things that I learned about Prez. So you know I’m drawn back to that. But I would say Stan Getz, Richie Kamuca, Lester Young for sure. I mean Prez, I copied a lot of Prez solos. And Gerry Mulligan was a huge influence on me, and all the guys that worked with Gerry Mulligan, because I bought all those albums, you know, “Ben Webster Meets Gerry Mulligan,” Johnny Hodges I used to copy Johnny Hodges’ solos. So all those guys were big influences. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-
